AMENDED_AFTER_SEEING_v1_NAIVE_OUTPUT_AND.what_the_amendment_could_NOT_touch_and_d: the ceiling, the random null, the k grid, n_draws, the seed, the declared family, and BOTH ARM LOCATIONS are byte-identical in v1 and v2 runs. The correction is confined to the naive arm.
AMENDED_AFTER_SEEING_v1_NAIVE_OUTPUT_AND.what_was_seen: v1's five naive capture points at all five k
AMENDED_AFTER_SEEING_v1_NAIVE_OUTPUT_AND.why_this_is_not_outcome_selection: the amendment removes an INSTRUMENT DEFECT -- an ordering that does not identify its own decline set -- and does not choose among outcomes. The tie treatment is applied to ALL five orderings by one rule, not to the ones whose numbers were disliked.

EVERYTHING_ELSE_CARRIES_FORWARD_UNCHANGE.pool: UNRESTRICTED, by R-518 -- never a preventable-restricted pool

INFORMATION_AT_DECISION_TIME_added_after.and_the_time_ordering_is_a_known_lever: a time ordering IS implementable as a decision-time gate (decline after T). That is LEVER T, which `policy_bounds_v1.py::bound_table` already bounds in this same tree -- so it is not a new lever, it is one with a bound already on it.
INFORMATION_AT_DECISION_TIME_added_after.the_point: a cancel is decided BEFORE the fill. Realised spread and realised size are POST-DECISION quantities. A naive ordering that beats a decision-time ranker using post-decision information is NOT an indictment of that ranker -- it is the oracle's error in a smaller size.
INFORMATION_AT_DECISION_TIME_added_after.why_it_is_flagged_as_late: this was NOT declared in advance. It is added because the results made it decisive, and it is labelled in the artifact so no reader takes it for a pre-registration.

falsifiers_added_both_ways: a strictly-ordered key must report tie share 0.0, a degenerate distribution and identified TRUE
a key that is ONE tied value must report tie share 1.0, identified FALSE, a positive spread, AND land where the random null lands -- because that is all it is
THE_TIE_TREATMENT.no_threshold_decides_the_treatment: an ordering with no boundary tie yields a degenerate distribution, which is its point. The same code path serves both.
THE_TIE_TREATMENT.ordering_is_identified: FALSE when more than half the decline set is chosen at the tied boundary. A not-identified ordering is reported and flagged, never quoted as a policy result.
THE_TIE_TREATMENT.rule: sort by the key; the fills STRICTLY better than the boundary value are taken whole; the remainder is DRAWN at random from the boundary tie group, n_draws times. A naive ordering therefore reports a DISTRIBUTION whose width is exactly the ambiguity in its own definition.
THE_TIE_TREATMENT.tie_decided_share_of_k: reported for every naive ordering in every cell

supersedes.why_the_pair: a bare filename cannot be verified and a resolver cannot follow it -- DE's resolver CRASHED on a bare-string supersedes (REV 54) and DA 91's census refuses to invent the link. Content is otherwise unchanged.

why_superseded: v1 declared the five naive orderings as DETERMINISTIC points. On the real book three of them are decided at a TIED key value. SIZE_LARGEST_FIRST is 100% TIE-DECIDED AT EVERY k -- 3,098 of the 4,315 fills have size exactly 5.0 -- so `argsort(kind='stable')` was returning the reference's iteration order, not a size ordering. It scored +1.29% / +1.15% / +0.90% and flipped sign twice across k, which is the signature of an arbitrary ordering. Those numbers are WITHDRAWN.
